title: Mixing: Mama’s Little Girl by Wings | 1972
content:
Control Room Four, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Alan Parsons

Wings’ song ‘Mama’s Little Girl’ was mixed in stereo on 13 December 1972.

This was the last of three consecutive mixing days for the Red Rose Speedway album, which also saw work done on ‘The Mess’ and ‘One More Kiss’. Only one of the songs made it onto the album.

Two stereo mixes of ‘Mama’s Little Girl’ were made, with the second temporarily marked best (new mixes were made on 5 February 1973). The song was being considered for a planned double album edition, but remained unreleased until 1990, when it was a b-side of Paul McCartney’s ‘Put It There’ single.

Towards the end of the session, studio engineer Alan Parsons assembled the mixes created so far, and four single-sided acetate discs were made for each member of Wings:

  • ‘Big Barn Bed’
  • ‘When The Night’
  • ‘Single Pigeon’
  • ‘Tragedy’
  • ‘Mama’s Little Girl’
  • ‘Loup (1st Indian On The Moon)’
  • ‘I Would Only Smile’
  • ‘Country Dreamer’
  • ‘Night Out’
  • ‘One More Kiss’
  • ‘Jazz Street’
  • ‘I Lie Around’
  • ‘Little Lamb Dragonfly’
  • ‘Get On The Right Thing’
  • ‘1882’ (live)
  • ‘The Mess’ (live)
  • ‘My Love’ (live)
  • ‘Seaside Woman’
  • ‘Best Friend’ (live)
  • Medley: ‘Hold Me Tight’/‘Lazy Dynamite’/‘Hands Of Love’/‘Power Cut’
